title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Mixed

After a period of sideways movement spanning the last two weeks, markets are now approaching a clear inflection point. Price action has tightened, volatility has contracted, and the major indices are consolidating in a narrowing range—typically a sign that a decisive move is nearing. From here, the setup could go one of two ways, and traders need to be ready for either.

In the bullish scenario, we see a clean breakout above the recent range highs. This would likely coincide with a surge in volume and expanding breadth—more stocks participating in the upside, more new highs, and stronger momentum across leadership names. A breakout of this kind could serve as the launchpad for the next leg up, potentially extending the rally for several weeks. Growth sectors like Technology and Consumer Discretionary, which have shown resilience during the consolidation, would likely resume leadership if this plays out. Should these signals appear, the environment would support scaling into high-quality setups and gradually increasing exposure, with stops placed under key support levels.

On the other hand, a failure to hold support—particularly a break below the 20-day moving average followed by a decisive move under the 50-day and prior pivot lows—would suggest distribution is taking over. This would signal a breakdown of the current consolidation and raise the odds of a deeper pullback or corrective phase. In this environment, failed breakouts, widening down-volume, and growing relative weakness in leading stocks would become red flags. If this scenario develops, the playbook shifts to defense: reduce position sizes, raise cash, cut exposure to names showing weakness, and wait for renewed signs of strength before reengaging.

Supporting this two-path framework is the internal health of the market, which currently reflects a state of mild optimism but lacks conviction. Breadth and momentum numbers are slightly positive, but they’ve yet to show the kind of robust expansion typically associated with strong upside moves. This reflects a market that has not yet committed to a direction—and is waiting for confirmation.

In the bullish case, we want to see:

  • An increase in the number of stocks making new 52-week highs

  • Rising momentum metrics (e.g., up-momentum stocks outpacing down-momentum)

  • Strength in risk-on sectors and participation from more stocks across market caps

In the bearish case, we’d see:

  • A rise in new lows and deterioration in up/down volume ratios

  • Breakdowns in previously strong leadership stocks

  • Increased correlation to downside moves across sectors

Risk Management and Exposure Control

Maintain a Constructively Bullish Stance:
The broader uptrend remains intact, with all major indices trading above their rising 20- and 50-day moving averages. While the past two weeks have seen a sideways chop, price has held key support, reflecting resilience. At this inflection point, maintain a bullish bias but be prepared to shift quickly if the market breaks to the downside. Use the 20-day MA and prior pivot lows as your key levels for risk management.

Scale Exposure Selectively:
Sideways action suggests a buildup of energy, making the next move critical. Focus on high-probability setups forming after recent consolidation—particularly names bouncing off the 10- or 20-day moving averages, or reclaiming support with volume. Avoid chasing strength; only commit to positions with tight risk control and clear technical structure.

Manage Weakness Actively:
Continue to reduce or exit positions that break down below support, lose relative strength, or show failed breakouts. Protect profits in extended names. Rotate into stocks or sectors demonstrating resilience within bases, particularly those showing strong accumulation while the broader market churns.

Market Monitoring and Internal Indicators

Key Moving Averages as Risk Gauges:
All major indices remain above their 20- and 50-day MAs—important technical thresholds. Watch these levels closely. A break below them, especially with volume and undercutting of prior lows, would shift the outlook toward caution and demand a more defensive posture.

Breadth and Momentum Are at a Crossroads:
Internals have stabilized but are not convincingly strong. Breadth and momentum metrics remain slightly positive—enough to support the uptrend, but not enough to confirm it. If we break to the upside, look for confirmation via expanding new highs and strong up/down volume. If the market breaks down, expect new lows and declining momentum to confirm that move.

Watch for Early Warnings:
Remain vigilant for internal divergences—failed breakouts, increasing down volume, or narrowing leadership. These may signal a downside resolution. Conversely, a broadening of participation and volume expansion would validate an upside breakout.

Sector and Theme Development

Lean on Resilient Growth Sectors:
Technology and Consumer Discretionary continue to lead and have held up well during this period of digestion. Their steady behavior supports continued institutional interest. Focus on semiconductors, software, and select retail names consolidating constructively near support.

Avoid Defensive Laggards:
Utilities, Energy, and Healthcare continue to underperform, reflecting a risk-on environment—so far. Avoid these areas unless they begin to show base-building with improving volume and RS.

Scan for Rotation Candidates:
Stay alert for early signs of rotation. Some Financials and Industrials are forming constructive bases and may lead if growth sectors rest. Look for higher lows, narrowing price action, and early breakouts to signal rotation into new leadership.

Capital Allocation and Trade Execution

Focus on Setup Quality:
In a market near a decision point, setup quality is paramount. Prioritize clean technical patterns near the 20-day MA, volume-supported breakouts, and reclaiming of support with improving RS. Avoid speculative or extended names—especially in the absence of strong internal confirmation.

Tighten Risk Controls:
Remain nimble. Position sizes should reflect current uncertainty. Use tighter stops and avoid overexposure until the market resolves decisively. Be quick to reduce risk on signs of breakdown or failed setups.

Preserve Cash Flexibility:
Keep cash available to act decisively once the market reveals its direction. A breakout could offer multiple opportunities in quick succession. A breakdown may require patience and capital preservation.

Daily Reassessment and Tactical Adjustments

Watch Behavior at Support and Resistance:
This week’s bounce off the 20-day MA is encouraging, but continuation is critical. A breakout from the two-week range with strong internals would justify increasing exposure. A breakdown through the 20-day and prior lows would shift the strategy to defense. Monitor both support and resistance levels closely for confirmation.

Let Setups Dictate Risk:
Only increase exposure if breakouts follow through with volume and breadth confirmation. If setups fail or stall, reduce risk and shift defensive. Let real-time price action—not bias—guide decisions.

Respond, Don’t Predict:
Markets are coiled, not committed. Avoid trying to guess the next move. Stay data-driven and responsive to actual market behavior. Flexibility and discipline will protect capital and position you for the next directional trend.

Key Focus Areas

  • Be Patient, Wait for Confirmation: Let the market resolve its current range before acting aggressively. Avoid overtrading in noise.

  • Track Sector Leadership Transitions: Maintain focus on Tech and Discretionary, but watch Financials and Industrials for emerging leadership.

  • Stay Tactical and Protect Gains: Keep exposure aligned with real-time strength. Use this period to defend capital and refine watchlists.

Bottom Line

The market has entered a pivotal zone after two weeks of tight consolidation. A breakout would offer opportunity for expanded exposure and fresh leadership, while a breakdown would demand caution. Internals are modestly supportive but not yet fully bullish. Maintain a constructively bullish posture—but operate with discipline: prioritize quality setups, keep risk tight, and be ready to pivot based on what the market confirms. Let price, volume, and internals—not predictions—drive your next move.
